Let agents source clips from terabytes of your local video

QDo I need the Clipto Mac app?

Yes. Clipto MCP uses the Clipto Mac app as the local media memory engine. Install Clipto first, then connect your AI tool.

QCan AI tools see all my files?

No. AI tools can only request results from Clipto based on the folders you approve. They do not get open-ended access to your Mac.

QDoes Clipto upload my original videos?

No by default. Clipto is designed around local-first media understanding, so your source media stays on your device unless you explicitly choose another workflow.

Clipto is designed for local media workflows. AI tools can ask Clipto for moments and context, but they do not get open-ended access to your Mac

Right now, it runs best on Apple Silicon Macs with 24GB+ memory, but we are working on broader support as well as an API/MCP for other agents to call.

We’d love to hear your feedback. Feel free to ask anything!

Motivation: we probably all had this similar experience, we know a moment exists in a video or audio, but finding it takes hours scrubbing the timeline. You can send all the media to process in the cloud, but it’s slow, expensive and raises privacy concerns. So we decided to build our own on-device media search engine.

How it works (high level):

1. We ingest video, audio, image; normalize formats via ffmpeg; run content analysis to downsample the frames for deeper understanding. [...] Right now, it runs best on Apple Silicon Macs with 24GB+ memory, but we are working on broader support as well as an API/MCP for other agents to call.

We’d love to hear your feedback. Feel free to ask anything!

How it works (high level):

1. We ingest video, audio, image; normalize formats via ffmpeg; run content analysis to downsample the frames for deeper understanding.

2. A local ASR pipeline (optimized Whisper) transcribes speech into text and speakers are identified; faces are detected and if known, person id created; a vision model (optimized Qwen3.5) runs on the downsampled frames to detect scenes, actions, objects, OCR and visual descriptions.

3. A graph data structure ties everything together into a searchable memory. [...] 4. At runtime, user’s query and intention are understood by a lightweight local language model. Graph search conducted to retrieve all the matching clip candidates and reranking is done by a reranking model.

5. All the processes are done on your computer, without touching our servers.

Right now, it runs best on Apple Silicon Macs with 24GB+ memory, but we are working on broader support as well as an API/MCP for other agents to call.

We’d love to hear your feedback. Feel free to ask anything!

Your Memory shouldn't begin with an upload. Your videos shouldn't leave your device just to become searchable. Your conversations shouldn't have to live in the cloud before AI can understand them.
